     6	
     7	# Data Visualization Skill
     8	
     9	Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.
    10	
    11	## Chart Selection Guide
    12	
    13	### Choose by Data Relationship
    14	
    15	| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
    18	| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
    19	| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
    20	| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
    21	| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
    22	| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
    23	| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
    24	| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
    25	| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
    26	| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
    27	| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
    28	| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
    29	| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |
    30	
    31	### When NOT to Use Certain Charts
    32	
    33	- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
    34	- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
    35	- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
    36	- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
    37	- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.
    38	
    39	## Python Visualization Code Patterns
    40	
    41	### Setup and Style
    42	
    43	```python

    54	    'figure.dpi': 150,
    55	    'font.size': 11,
    56	    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    57	    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',

   189	### Number Formatting Helpers
   190	
   191	```python
   192	def format_number(val, format_type='number'):
   193	    """Format numbers for chart labels."""
   194	    if format_type == 'currency':
   195	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   196	            return f'${val/1e9:.1f}B'
   197	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   198	            return f'${val/1e6:.1f}M'
   199	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   200	            return f'${val/1e3:.1f}K'
   201	        else:
   202	            return f'${val:,.0f}'
   203	    elif format_type == 'percent':
   204	        return f'{val:.1f}%'
   205	    elif format_type == 'number':
   206	        if abs(val) >= 1e9:
   207	            return f'{val/1e9:.1f}B'
   208	        elif abs(val) >= 1e6:
   209	            return f'{val/1e6:.1f}M'
   210	        elif abs(val) >= 1e3:
   211	            return f'{val/1e3:.1f}K'
   212	        else:
   213	            return f'{val:,.0f}'
   214	    return str(val)
   215	
   216	# Usage with axis formatter
   217	ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: format_number(x, 'currency')))
   218	```

   241	## Design Principles
   242	
   243	### Color
   244	
   245	- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
   246	- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
   247	- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
   248	- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
   249	- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
   250	- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair
   251	
   252	### Typography
   253	
   254	- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
   255	- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
   256	- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
   257	- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
   258	- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations
   259	
   260	### Layout
   261	
   262	- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
   263	- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
   264	- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
   265	- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe
   266	
   267	### Accuracy
   268	
   269	- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
   270	- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
   271	- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
   272	- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
   273	- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean
   274	
   275	## Accessibility Considerations
   276	
   277	### Color Blindness
   278	
   279	- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
   280	- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
   281	- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
   282	- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`
   283	
   284	### Screen Readers
   285	
   286	- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
   287	- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
   288	- Use semantic titles and labels
   289	
   290	### General Accessibility
   291	
   292	- Sufficient contrast between data elements and background
   293	- Text size minimum 10pt for labels, 12pt for titles
   294	- Avoid conveying information only through spatial position (add labels)
   295	- Consider printing: does the chart work in black and white?
   296	
   297	### Accessibility Checklist
   298	
   299	Before sharing a visualization:
   300	- [ ] Chart works without color (patterns, labels, or line styles differentiate series)
   301	- [ ] Text is readable at standard zoom level
   302	- [ ] Title describes the insight, not just the data
   303	- [ ] Axes are labeled with units
   304	- [ ] Legend is clear and positioned without obscuring data
   305	- [ ] Data source and date range are noted

1	# AI Model Capability Benchmark Data
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Normalized benchmark scores for 10 large language models across 8 capability dimensions, designed for parallel coordinates visualization. Models span 5 families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen) with both flagship and lightweight variants per family.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### model_benchmarks
     9	Each record represents one AI model with the following fields:
    10	- **model** (string): Model name, e.g., "GPT-4o", "Claude 3.5 Sonnet"
    11	- **family** (string): Model family grouping — one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Qwen
    12	- **Reasoning** (integer, 0-100): Complex multi-step reasoning benchmark score
    13	- **Code Generation** (integer, 0-100): Programming and code synthesis score
    14	- **Math / Quantitative** (integer, 0-100): Mathematical problem-solving score
    15	- **Language Understanding** (integer, 0-100): NLU and reading comprehension score
    16	- **Multimodal Understanding** (integer, 0-100): Image, video, and cross-modal reasoning score
    17	- **Instruction Following** (integer, 0-100): Adherence to complex user instructions
    18	- **Inference Speed** (integer, 0-100): Normalized throughput (higher = faster)
    19	- **Knowledge Recall** (integer, 0-100): Factual knowledge and world knowledge retrieval
    20	
    21	All scores are normalized to a 0-100 scale for cross-dimension comparability.
    22	
    23	## Data Notes
    24	- Scores are synthetic composites inspired by publicly reported benchmarks (MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, MMMU, MT-Bench, etc.) but do not correspond to exact published numbers.
    25	- Inference Speed is inversely related to model size; lightweight variants score higher.
    26	- Multimodal scores for text-only-focused models (LLaMA, Qwen) are notably lower, reflecting limited native multimodal capability.
    27	- Each family includes one flagship and one smaller/faster variant to illustrate capability-efficiency trade-offs.

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

models = data['model_benchmarks']['data']
dimensions = data['model_benchmarks']['dimensions']

# Family color mapping (per task spec)
family_colors = {
    'GPT': '#4C72B0',      # blue
    'Claude': '#8172B3',   # purple
    'Gemini': '#55A868',   # green
    'LLaMA': '#DD8452',    # orange
    'Qwen': '#C44E52',     # red
}

# Compute average score per model for prominence
for m in models:
    m['avg_score'] = np.mean([m[d] for d in dimensions])

# Sort models so top performers draw on top (higher avg = later = on top)
# Also group by family for visual cohesion
models_sorted = sorted(models, key=lambda x: (x['family'], x['avg_score']))

# Identify top models (top 3 by avg score)
top_models = {m['model'] for m in sorted(models, key=lambda x: x['avg_score'], reverse=True)[:3]}

# Style setup: data-dense, publication-ready
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (14, 7),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 9,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

fig, ax = plt.subplots()

# Axes positions
x_pos = np.arange(len(dimensions))

# Draw axes first (background)
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.text(i, -5, dim, ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', wrap=True)

# Draw y ticks and labels on the first axis only to reduce clutter
ax.set_yticks([0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100])
ax.set_yticklabels(['0', '20', '40', '60', '80', '100'])
ax.set_ylim(-12, 108)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(dimensions) - 0.5)

# Draw horizontal grid lines
for y in [0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]:
    ax.axhline(y=y, color='#e0e0e0', linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)

# Plot each model
for m in models_sorted:
    y_vals = [m[d] for d in dimensions]
    color = family_colors[m['family']]
    is_top = m['model'] in top_models
    
    # Top models: thicker, more opaque, slightly brighter
    linewidth = 2.5 if is_top else 1.5
    alpha = 0.95 if is_top else 0.55
    linestyle = '-' if is_top else '-'
    
    ax.plot(x_pos, y_vals, color=color, linewidth=linewidth,
            alpha=alpha, linestyle=linestyle, solid_capstyle='round', zorder=2 if is_top else 1)
    
    # Add small dot markers for top models
    if is_top:
        ax.scatter(x_pos, y_vals, color=color, s=30, zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)

# Highlight specific crossing regions with subtle background shading
# Reasoning (0) vs Inference Speed (6) crossing emphasis
ax.axvspan(-0.25, 0.25, alpha=0.06, color='#4C72B0', zorder=0)
ax.axvspan(5.75, 6.25, alpha=0.06, color='#4C72B0', zorder=0)

# Multimodal (4) vs Math (2) divergence emphasis
ax.axvspan(1.75, 2.25, alpha=0.06, color='#55A868', zorder=0)
ax.axvspan(3.75, 4.25, alpha=0.06, color='#55A868', zorder=0)

# Annotations for key insights
ax.annotate('High reasoning →\nLow speed tradeoff',
            xy=(3, 50), fontsize=8, ha='center', va='center',
            color='#444444', style='italic',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f8f8f8', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.8))

ax.annotate('Multimodal ↔ Math\ndivergence',
            xy=(3, 30), fontsize=8, ha='center', va='center',
            color='#444444', style='italic',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#f8f8f8', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.8))

# Legend: family patches + top model indicator
legend_patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=family_colors[f], label=f) for f in family_colors]
legend_patches.append(mpatches.Patch(color='#888888', label='Top models (thicker)'))

ax.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc='upper right', frameon=True,
          fancybox=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor='#cccccc', ncol=1)

# Title and subtitle
ax.set_title('AI Model Capability Profiles Across 8 Benchmark Dimensions', fontweight='bold', pad=20)
fig.text(0.5, 0.94, 'Normalized scores (0–100). Thicker lines highlight top-performing models. '
         'Crossing patterns reveal capability–speed trade-offs.',
         ha='center', va='top', fontsize=9, color='#555555')

# Remove spines
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_linewidth(0.8)
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#999999')

# X-axis labels already drawn manually; hide default x ticks
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_ylabel('Normalized Score', fontsize=10)

# Source note
fig.text(0.5, 0.01, 'Source: Composite benchmark data (synthetic composites inspired by MMLU, HumanEval, GSM8K, MMMU, MT-Bench).',
         ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=7, color='#888888')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.92])
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.close()
print('Saved /app/output/result.png')
